goal: Run automated weekly discovery and publish only unique, date-stamped items with clickable source links into docs/reports.json.
principles: Do not publish the same article in more than one module; assign each item to the single best-fit module.
Each module should target at least five unique items; prefer recency over quota filling.
If the latest 14 days do not provide enough strong items, expand to 30 days, then 90 days, and keep the published date visible.

Academic discovery should not be US-only; prioritize strong research countries and domain leaders, including France, Germany, Japan, South Korea, the EU, UK, Singapore, Switzerland, and Nordic countries when topic fit is strong.
Industry and policy discovery should overweight China, especially government, regulator, standards, filing, raw-material specification, and official policy releases.

Competitor searches must start from the A-level watchlist and prioritize official sites, official accounts, regulatory records, clinical registrations, patents, product evidence pages, credible commercial observation, and authoritative science communication.

AI industry discovery should include OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepMind, NVIDIA, Microsoft, research labs, investor/news releases, developer blogs, technical magazines, institution reports, and founder/developer interviews.

Books, documentaries, films, long interviews, and podcasts can enter a recommendation card only when author/director/speaker, country or region, date, focus section, excerpt or key moment, inspiration, and clickable source are available.
Marketing-only reposts, unsourced commentary, broken links, and duplicate syndications must not enter docs/reports.json.
